sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History, which comes, not inappropriately, from Greece, or at least partly from Greece.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余烬》（The Rest is History）。本期节目非常应景地从希腊录制，至少部分是在希腊录制的。

sentences.en: The historian Herodotus tells the story of the Battle of Thermopylae, when the Spartans made their heroic stand against the Persian king Xerxes.
sentences.zh: 历史学家希罗多德讲述了温泉关战役的故事，当时斯巴达人对阵波斯国王薛西斯，进行了英勇的抵抗。

sentences.en: And afterwards, when the Persians had wiped the floor with the Spartans, they asked a group of Greek deserters why there were so few Greeks at the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 事后，当波斯人把斯巴达人杀得片甲不留时，他们问了一群希腊逃兵，为什么战场上只有那么点希腊人。

sentences.en: And the deserters supposedly replied that the rest of the Greeks were off at the Olympic Games watching the horse racing.
sentences.zh: 据说那些逃兵回答说，剩下的希腊人都跑去参加奥林匹克运动会看赛马了。

sentences.en: The Persians asked, what was their prize?
sentences.zh: 波斯人问，奖品是什么？

sentences.en: What was the point?
sentences.zh: 意义何在？

sentences.en: And the Greeks said the prize was a crown of olive leaves.
sentences.zh: 希腊人说，奖品是一顶橄榄枝编成的桂冠。

sentences.en: And at that, the Persians supposedly cried out and gnashed their teeth and rent their garments and said, what kind of men are these that we're fighting against?
sentences.zh: 听到这话，波斯人据说大声痛哭、咬牙切齿、撕裂衣衫，然后说道：我们面对的究竟是一群什么样的人啊？

sentences.en: They fight not for riches, but for glory.
sentences.zh: 他们战斗不是为了财富，而是为了荣耀。

sentences.en: Now, another person who fights only for glory is my collaborator, Tom Holland, the translator of Herodotus' histories, no less.
sentences.zh: 现在，另一个只为荣耀而战的人就是我的合作者汤姆·霍兰，他正是希罗多德《历史》的译者。

sentences.en: Tom, you're very keen on the Olympics, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你对奥运会非常热衷，对吧？

sentences.en: I imagine you're dying to see the kickoff in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 我想你一定迫不及待地想看东京奥运会的开幕了。

sentences.en: You can't wait.
sentences.zh: 你简直等不及了。

sentences.en: Well, I'm very keen on the ancient Olympics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对古代奥运会非常热衷。

sentences.en: I actually find the modern ones a bit boring, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，其实我觉得现代奥运会有点无聊。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The synchronized swimming doesn't do it for you or the powerlifting or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 花样游泳没法吸引你，还是说举重之类的东西？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 倒也不是。

sentences.en: But the ancient ones are fantastic.
sentences.zh: 但古代奥运会太棒了。

sentences.en: And I'm incredibly jealous of you being in Greece right now as we record this.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在录制节目的这一刻，你身在希腊，我真是嫉妒得要命。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And very grateful that you have broken off from downing Retzina in the shade of Nicene, fleshpots of Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你在尼西内的阴凉处、拿破仑的纵欲之乡畅饮雷奇纳葡萄酒时，能抽空连线。

sentences.en: In the fleshpots of the Peloponnese.
sentences.zh: 是在伯罗奔尼撒的纵欲之乡。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what have you done?
sentences.zh: 那你都干了些什么？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I've broken off my holiday to be lectured by you about ancient religion.
sentences.zh: 我打断了假期，来听你给我上关于古代宗教的课。

sentences.en: And I said to my wife, as she went off taking my son for an ice cream, I said, basically, for the next hour,
sentences.zh: 我对妻子说，当她带着我儿子去买冰淇淋时，我跟她说，基本上在接下来的一小时里，

sentences.en: Tom Holland will be just using the word sacral again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰会一遍又一遍、没完没了地使用“神圣的”这个词。

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我确实会。

sentences.en: I know exactly what's coming.
sentences.zh: 我太清楚接下来要发生什么了。

sentences.en: You know me too well.
sentences.zh: 你太了解我了。

sentences.en: Before we get on to the sacral quality of the ancient Olympic Games, and I'm like, wow, am I going to major on that?
sentences.zh: 在我们探讨古代奥运会的神圣属性之前——我心里想，哇，我要重点讲这个吗？

sentences.en: But have you, you haven't actually been to Olympia, though, this summer?
sentences.zh: 不过你，今年夏天你其实并没有去过奥林匹亚，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Although, I've never been.
sentences.zh: 虽然我从来没去过。

sentences.en: Although yesterday we went to Namia, which is another Games location.
sentences.zh: 不过昨天我们去了尼米亚，那是另一个运动会的举办地。

sentences.en: And so there's a brilliant tunnel.
sentences.zh: 那里有一条绝妙的隧道。

sentences.en: They've sort of reconstructed, I think, the tunnel that the athletes, it's very like, you know, stepping onto the field for the World Cup final or something.
sentences.zh: 他们好像重建了运动员走的那条隧道，那种感觉就像，你知道的，踏上世界杯决赛的球场一样。

sentences.en: And then you go through the tunnel and you emerge into the stadium and, yeah, you get a fantastic sense of what it was like.
sentences.zh: 然后你穿过隧道，走进体育场，接着，是的，你会对当年的情景有一种奇妙的感受。

sentences.en: I mean, I know that's a silly thing to say because you don't really know what it was like, but you can sort of pretend anyway.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道这么说很傻，因为你根本不知道当时是什么样的，但你至少可以假装一下。

sentences.en: I played the final countdown on my phone and got my son to run through the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 我在手机上播放了最后的倒计时，让我儿子跑着穿过了隧道。

sentences.en: Because, of course, there's nobody else here because of COVID.
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，由于疫情，那里空无一人。

sentences.en: So it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以这太棒了。

sentences.en: You get it all to yourself.
sentences.zh: 整个地方全归你了。

sentences.en: And you win the crown.
sentences.zh: 然后你赢得了桂冠。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The olive wreath.
sentences.zh: 橄榄花环。

sentences.en: So you mentioned the Nemean Games.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了尼米亚竞技会。

sentences.en: Yeah, there were four, weren't there?
sentences.zh: 对，有四个，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, there are lots of games, but there are four games where basically, as in the story that you read from Herodotus, you get a crown.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多竞技会有四个，基本上就像你从希罗多德那里读到的故事一样，你能赢得一顶桂冠。

sentences.en: So they're called the Stefanik Games.
sentences.zh: 所以它们被称为司提方竞技会（Stephani Games）。

sentences.en: Stefanos being Greek for a crown.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬斯（Stefanos）在希腊语中是桂冠的意思。

sentences.en: So the Nemean Games was basically ranked fourth.
sentences.zh: 所以尼米亚竞技会的排名基本上是第四。

sentences.en: Oh, you're telling me I've been to the – I didn't even get on the podium.
sentences.zh: 哦，你是在告诉我，我去的这个——我甚至连领奖台都没登上。

sentences.en: Yeah, you didn't even podium.
sentences.zh: 对，你甚至都没进前三（podium）。

sentences.en: The Nemean Games and not even the bronze medal of games.
sentences.zh: 尼米亚竞技会连铜牌都算不上。

sentences.en: That's so disappointing.
sentences.zh: 太令人失望了。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: The Isomian.
sentences.zh: 地峡竞技会（Isthmian）。

sentences.en: The Isomian is the bronze one.
sentences.zh: 地峡竞技会是铜牌级别的。

sentences.en: So that's a Corinth.
sentences.zh: 那是科林斯举办的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The Isomian is joining the Peloponnese, the southern kind of fork of Greece to the mainland.
sentences.zh: 地峡竞技会连接着伯罗奔尼撒，即希腊南部的那个分叉与大陆。

sentences.en: Then the Pythian, which is at Delphi.
sentences.zh: 然后是皮托竞技会（Pythian），在德尔斐。

sentences.en: And then the Olympian.
sentences.zh: 最后是奥林匹克竞技会。

sentences.en: And Pausanias, who is second century AD, basically he kind of writes travel guides.
sentences.zh: 保萨尼亚斯生活在公元二世纪，他基本上算是写旅游指南的。

sentences.en: He writes a travel guide to Greece.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本希腊旅游指南。

sentences.en: The Rough Guide.
sentences.zh: 《Rough Guide》旅游指南。

sentences.en: The Rough Guide.
sentences.zh: 《粗略指南》

sentences.en: And he says of the Olympic Games, they are the greatest, the greatest of games.
sentences.zh: 他这样评价奥林匹克运动会：它们是最伟大的，所有运动会中最伟大的。

sentences.en: And so that's why the modern games are named after them, because they are the pinnacle.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么现代运动会以它们命名，因为它们是巅峰。

sentences.en: Well, did Pausanias – you're not claiming that he invented the idea that the Olympic Games were the beSt.
sentences.zh: 那么保萨尼亚斯——你不是在断言是他发明了“奥运会是最好的”这种观点吧？

sentences.en: I mean, were they genuinely the best and the greatest?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们真的是最好、最伟大的吗？

sentences.en: No, he said that they rank firSt.
sentences.zh: 不，他说它们排名第一。

sentences.en: They come top.
sentences.zh: 它们位居榜首。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If you win at the Olympic Games, then that's absolutely the beSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你在奥运会上获胜，那绝对是最好的。

sentences.en: Although the mark of a really elite athlete, and you know how keen I am on elite sport, is to get the Grand Slam.
sentences.zh: 尽管真正精英运动员的标志——你知道我多么热衷于精英体育——是赢得大满贯。

sentences.en: A bit like kind of tennis now.
sentences.zh: 有点像现在的网球那样。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, what Nero did, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，尼禄就是这么干的，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I'm sure we'll come to this later on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确信我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: That is what Nero did.
sentences.zh: 尼禄确实这么干过。

sentences.en: But – and I know how much you've been looking forward to me using the word sacral.
sentences.zh: 但是——而且我知道你有多么期待我使用“神圣的”这个词。

sentences.en: Yes, come on.
sentences.zh: 是的，来吧。

sentences.en: Let's get it over with.
sentences.zh: 咱们快把它说出来吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the key – really, the fundamental difference between the modern Olympic Games, which, as constituted now, is basically about money.
sentences.zh: 所以关键——实际上，现代奥运会与古代奥运会的根本区别在于，现代奥运会（按目前的组织形式）基本上关乎金钱。

sentences.en: I mean, the reason that they're going ahead in a time of COVID, it's not because of the Olympic spirit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们之所以能在疫情期间继续举行，不是因为奥运精神。

sentences.en: It's not because of the amity of nations.
sentences.zh: 不是因为国家间的友谊。

sentences.en: It's because of TV deals.
sentences.zh: 而是因为电视转播协议。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, we're going to do the modern Olympics, aren't we, in another podcast, so we can do all the sleaze and the politics of it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们会在另一期播客里专门聊聊现代奥运会，对吧？这样我们就可以大谈其中的卑劣勾当和政治了。

sentences.en: But the episode you mentioned with Thermopylae, the Persians are invading Greece.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才提到的温泉关那个插曲，波斯人正在入侵希腊。

sentences.en: This is a massive crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的危机。

sentences.en: Holding the pass at Thermopylae is the best option the Greeks have to stop the Persian advance.
sentences.zh: 死守温泉关是希腊人阻止波斯人推进的最佳选择。

sentences.en: But they don't go because of the Games.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有去，因为要办运动会。

sentences.en: And that's not because they're obsessed by sport, although they are.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为他们对体育着迷，尽管他们的确着迷。

sentences.en: It's because the Olympic Games have this incredible status as something that is holy to the gods.
sentences.zh: 而是因为奥运会在神明面前拥有难以置信的神圣地位。

sentences.en: And so, again, Pausanias, when he goes to Olympia and he says about the Games that there are basically the two holiest events in Greece.
sentences.zh: 所以，保萨尼亚斯再次提到，当他去奥林匹亚谈到运动会时，那里基本上是希腊最神圣的两大活动之一。

sentences.en: One is the mysteries at Eleusis, which is just outside Athens,
sentences.zh: 一个是厄琉息斯秘仪，就在雅典城外，

sentences.en: where it's involved with the story of Demeter and Persephone and Persephone going into the underworld and then coming back for six months and going back.
sentences.zh: 那里涉及得墨忒耳和珀耳塞福涅的故事，珀耳塞福涅进入冥界，然后回来待六个月，接着又回去。

sentences.en: And it's all basically about life and death.
sentences.zh: 这基本上全关于生死。

sentences.en: So it's absolutely at the heart of everything that a mortal might want to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以它绝对是一个凡人可能想要了解的一切事物的核心。

sentences.en: But he says that the Olympics, the Olympic Games are, the festival of the Olympics are on that level.
sentences.zh: 但他说，奥运会，奥林匹克运动会的庆典达到了那个级别。

sentences.en: And actually, when I say Olympic Games as a synonym for festival, that's wrong, because the Games are only a part of the broader festival.
sentences.zh: 实际上，当我把奥运会当作庆典的同义词时，这是不对的，因为运动会只是更广泛庆典的一部分。

sentences.en: Let's go back to the origins.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到起源。

sentences.en: So when did they, the conventional date is 776, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以它们的起源，传统日期是公元前776年，对吧？

sentences.en: And we get that from Aristotle, am I right, that he says it was 776 BC?
sentences.zh: 我们是从亚里士多德那里得知这一点的，我没记错吧，他说那是公元前776年？

sentences.en: Yes, well, we get it also from a guy called Hippias of Elis.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我们也是从一个叫伊利斯的希庇亚斯的人那里知道的。

sentences.en: And Elis is the kind of the town that over the course of history comes to kind of monopolize and lay claim to the Games and the festival.
sentences.zh: 伊利斯是这样一个城镇：在历史长河中，它逐渐垄断并宣称拥有运动会和庆典的主办权。

sentences.en: And essentially, if you win the sprint, which is the first race, and it's won by this butcher, supposedly, called Koroibus.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你赢得了短跑比赛，也就是第一场比赛，据说获胜者是一个名叫科洛伊布斯的屠夫。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Then from that point on, your name as the guy who wins the sprint, this is how the Greeks date.
sentences.zh: 那么从那一刻起，赢得短跑比赛的你的名字——希腊人就是这样记年代的。

sentences.en: This is the dating system that they use.
sentences.zh: 这是他们使用的纪年系统。

sentences.en: So it's kind of, I mean, how elite is that?
sentences.zh: 所以这简直是——我的意思是，这有多精英？

sentences.en: You win a sprint and then your name, you know, is going to be used forever after by people drawing up histories.
sentences.zh: 你赢得了一场短跑比赛，然后你的名字，你知道的，将被后世撰写历史的人永远使用下去。

sentences.en: Well, just to interject on this, we were in Sparta the other day, in modern Sparta, which, as my son said, is not, it doesn't quite live up to his image of ancient Sparta.
sentences.zh: 好吧，插话一下，我们前几天在斯巴达，现代的斯巴达，正如我儿子所说，它不太符合他对古代斯巴达的想象。

sentences.en: But in the middle of modern Sparta, there is a monument, an Olympic monument, and it has the names of every Spartan who won the Olympics, going back to, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是在现代斯巴达的市中心，有一座纪念碑，一座奥运纪念碑，上面刻着每一个赢得过奥运会冠军的斯巴达人的名字，可以追溯到，你知道的，

sentences.en: the 8th century BC or whatever it is, and going right up to the early 21st century.
sentences.zh: 公元前8世纪左右，一直延续到21世纪初。

sentences.en: And I thought, I mean, they're basically pretending there's no break.
sentences.zh: 我想，我的意思是，他们基本上在假装中间没有任何中断。

sentences.en: They're pretending that the Olympic Games are the same thing and that's Sparta.
sentences.zh: 他们假装奥运会一直是同一回事，这就是斯巴达。

sentences.en: So I loved that, that that was a sort of, that they're still remembering these guys, you know, 2,500 years ago,
sentences.zh: 所以我很喜欢这一点，他们仍然在缅怀这些家伙，你知道的，2500年前的人，

sentences.en: and they still got this sort of monument to their Spartan Olympic heroes.
sentences.zh: 并且他们仍然为自己的斯巴达奥运英雄保留着这样一座纪念碑。

sentences.en: So the names do live forevermore.
sentences.zh: 所以这些名字确实流芳百世了。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对如此。

sentences.en: And so Greek contenders knew that, I mean, the fame that you win is, in a sense, the kind of the key to it.
sentences.zh: 因此，希腊的竞争者们深知这一点，我的意思是，你赢得的名声在某种程度上就是这一切的关键。

sentences.en: But, it won't surprise you to know that there are complications.
sentences.zh: 但是，你不会感到惊讶的是，其中有一些复杂情况。

sentences.en: So one of them is, you know, is this true?
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: And actually, the kind of the weight of opinion is probably that it vaguely is.
sentences.zh: 实际上，主流观点可能认为它大致上是真的。

sentences.en: Well, the butcher did win, and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那个屠夫确实赢了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, perhaps, who knows?
sentences.zh: 是的，也许吧，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I mean, we've got no way, really, of knowing, but it seems feasible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们真的无从知晓，但它似乎是可信的。

sentences.en: But this kind of, you know, we can recognise that that's a historical account.
sentences.zh: 但这种——你知道的，我们可以承认这是一个历史叙事。

sentences.en: But for the Greeks, and I'm afraid I'm going to use the word, the sacral quality of the game.
sentences.zh: 但对希腊人来说——恐怕我要用那个词了——运动会的神圣属性。

sentences.en: Here we go, yeah.
sentences.zh: 来了，是的。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you did that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我太高兴你这么说了，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, it would be disappointing if you didn't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你不说，那才叫人失望呢。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: There's interwoven with myth.
sentences.zh: 这里面交织着神话。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And so you can basically, with the Greeks, you can hold, you know, kind of three or four ideas simultaneously in your head.
sentences.zh: 所以对于希腊人，你基本上可以同时在脑海中容纳三到四种不同的观念。

sentences.en: So you can have this idea that there is a kind of recognisable starting point, that you get on the blocks, you know, firing gun goes, and you're off.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以这样认为：有一个可识别的起跑线，你站上起跑器，你知道的，发令枪响，然后你出发了。

sentences.en: The games have begun.
sentences.zh: 运动会已经开始了。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you also have to kind of enmesh it in your ideas about the stories told of the gods and the heroes.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你还得把它与你对神明和英雄传说的理解交织在一起。

sentences.en: And as is always the way with Greece, there is no definitive account.
sentences.zh: 就像希腊一贯的方式那样，没有一个绝对权威的说法。

sentences.en: So it's held at Olympia.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在奥林匹亚举办的。

sentences.en: Olympia, obviously, there's the resonance with Olympus, the home of the gods, where Zeus, the king of the gods, rules.
sentences.zh: 奥林匹亚，显而易见，这让人联想到奥林匹斯山，那是神明的居所，众神之王宙斯在那里统治。

sentences.en: And it's...
sentences.zh: 而且它……

sentences.en: Is it named after Olympus, Tom?
sentences.zh: 它是以奥林匹斯命名的吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Is it named after Mount Olympus, the place?
sentences.zh: 它是以奥林匹斯山这个地方命名的吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's named after Olympian Zeus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是以奥林匹亚的宙斯命名的。

sentences.en: So Zeus presides over the games.
sentences.zh: 所以是宙斯主持这些运动会。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, one of the stories that's told about the origins of the games, and again, going back to Pausanias, who really is a kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，关于运动会起源的传说之一——同样可以追溯到保萨尼亚斯，他其实算是那种，你知道的

sentences.en: the crucial source for this.
sentences.zh: 这方面的关键史料来源。

sentences.en: He says, some say Zeus wrestled there at Olympia with Kronos himself for the throne of heaven.
sentences.zh: 他说，有人说宙斯当年就是在奥林匹亚与克罗诺斯本人摔跤，为的是争夺天堂的王座。

sentences.en: Some say he held the games as a celebration of his triumph.
sentences.zh: 有人说他举办运动会是为了庆祝自己的胜利。

sentences.en: And Kronos was Zeus's father, who swallowed, who, you know, there was a prediction that he would be toppled by his child.
sentences.zh: 克罗诺斯是宙斯的父亲，他曾吞下……你知道的，当时有预言说他会被自己的孩子推翻。

sentences.en: And so he devours his children as they're born.
sentences.zh: 所以他把自己的孩子一出生就吞进肚子里。

sentences.en: And he gets tricked because Zeus's mother gives him a stone, gives him a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes.
sentences.zh: 但他被骗了，因为宙斯的母亲给了他一块石头，一块用襁褓裹着的石头。

sentences.en: And Zeus is then able to live and comes and defeats him.
sentences.zh: 于是宙斯得以存活，并最终前来打败了他。

sentences.en: So that is kind of pinning the origins of the Olympics right to the beginning of the reign of the Olympians, the coming of the Olympians.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比把奥运会的起源直接锚定在了奥林匹斯神统治的开端，也就是奥林匹斯诸神的降临。

sentences.en: So that's the kind of measure of its significance.
sentences.zh: 这就是衡量其重要性的方式。

sentences.en: But, Tom, I read this story.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，我读到过这样一个故事。

sentences.en: I read it only today that Pelops, the son of Tantalus, a man who had survived being eaten by the gods, being served to the gods as food by his own father,
sentences.zh: 我今天才读到，坦塔ロス的儿子珀罗普斯——这个人曾险遭神明吃掉，被他亲生父亲当成食物端给众神，

sentences.en: which is not a claim many of us can make.
sentences.zh: 这可不是我们大多数人敢吹嘘的经历。

sentences.en: But he had done this and lived to tell the tale,
sentences.zh: 但他确实经历过并活了下来，还把故事讲了出去——

sentences.en: that he had a chariot race with his prospective father-in-law in which he replaced the linchpins and the wheels of his father-in-law's chariot with wax.
sentences.zh: 说他曾与未来的岳父进行了一场战车比赛，比赛中他把自己岳父战车的销钉和车轮换成了蜡制的。

sentences.en: So they melted and he died.
sentences.zh: 结果蜡融化了，他岳父就死了。

sentences.en: And he then held funeral games to remember his father-in-law, which became the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 然后他举办了葬礼运动会来纪念岳父，这就演变成了奥运会。

sentences.en: Is that not the origin of the games?
sentences.zh: 难道这才是运动会的起源吗？

sentences.en: So that's another story.
sentences.zh: 所以这又是另一个故事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's the one that actually kind of wins.
sentences.zh: 而这才是那个真正占据主流的传说。

sentences.en: I say you can keep all these different ideas in your head.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以把所有这些不同的说法都记在脑子里。

sentences.en: So it matters to identify the origins with Zeus.
sentences.zh: 所以，将起源与宙斯联系起来是很重要的。

sentences.en: But, yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但是，没错，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Pelops, who gives his name to the Peloponnese, where you are sitting now.
sentences.zh: 珀罗普斯，伯罗奔尼撒正是因他而得名，也就是你现在坐的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And actually, there's a link to the Lucian mysteries there as well, because the one god who eats a bit of Pelops is Demeter, because she's in mourning for Persephone,
sentences.zh: 其实，这跟厄琉西斯秘仪也有渊源，因为吃掉珀罗普斯身上一小块肉的神正是德墨忒尔，当时她正在为珀耳塞福涅服丧，

sentences.en: who's just been abducted by Hades, the king of the underworld.
sentences.zh: 珀耳塞福涅刚刚被冥界之王哈迪斯绑架了。

sentences.en: And so from that point on, the gods kind of reconstitute him, bring him back to life.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，众神重塑了他的身体，让他复活了。

sentences.en: From that point on, he has an ivory shoulder to replace the bit that Demeter had snapped.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他有了一个象牙的肩膀，用来替代被德墨忒尔咬掉的那一部分。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 真酷。

sentences.en: So he's from Anatolia.
sentences.zh: 所以他是来自安纳托利亚。

sentences.en: He crosses Aegean.
sentences.zh: 他穿过爱琴海。

sentences.en: He comes to what will come to be called the Peloponnese, the island of Pelops.
sentences.zh: 他来到了后来被称为伯罗奔尼撒的地方，也就是珀罗普斯之岛。

sentences.en: And he goes to a place called Pisa, which isn't the place with the power in Italy.
sentences.zh: 他去了一个叫比萨的地方，可不是意大利那个有斜塔的地方。

sentences.en: It's about a mile from where Olympia will be.
sentences.zh: 它距离后来奥林匹亚所在地大约有一英里。

sentences.en: And absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Oinomaeus, who's the king there.
sentences.zh: 当时有个叫俄诺玛罗斯的人，是那里的国王。

sentences.en: And he has a daughter, Hippodamia.
sentences.zh: 他有一个女儿叫希波达米亚。

sentences.en: And a bit like Kronos having been told that he will be killed by a son.
sentences.zh: 有点像克罗诺斯曾被告知他会被儿子杀死一样。

sentences.en: Oinomaeus has been told that he will be killed by the man who marries his daughter.
sentences.zh: 俄诺玛罗斯也被预言说他会被娶他女儿的男人杀死。

sentences.en: And so he's not keen on this.
sentences.zh: 所以他对这事很不高兴。

sentences.en: And so every suitor, he challenges a suitor to a chariot race with the proviso that if the guy who wins the chariot race loses, he can be killed.
sentences.zh: 于是每一个求婚者，他都会向其发起战车比赛的挑战，条件是如果求婚者赢了战车赛还好，要是输了就会被处死。

sentences.en: And so Pelops arrives and they're welcoming him to Pisa above the palace of his prospective father-in-law, a kind of, you know, a rack of skulls, decaying heads,
sentences.zh: 所以当珀罗普斯抵达时，他们在他未来岳父宫殿上方欢迎他，呈现在眼前的，你知道的，是一排头骨，那些腐烂的脑袋，

sentences.en: the flesh dripping off.
sentences.zh: 血肉还在往下滴落。

sentences.en: A lot of us are very familiar with those kinds of scenes with our own father-in-law.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人对跟自己老丈人相处时的这种场景都非常熟悉。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he obviously is twitchy, but he's got advantages because he's got winged steeds that are a gift from the gods.
sentences.zh: 所以他显然有点紧张，但他有优势，因为他拥有神明赠予的带翅膀的神马。

sentences.en: So that's a kind of advantage.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种优势吧。

sentences.en: But he wants to make absolutely sure.
sentences.zh: 但他想做到万无一失。

sentences.en: And so he bribes his father, prospective father-in-law's charioteer, a guy called Myrtalos, to exactly, as you say, replace the spokes with the, what are they,
sentences.zh: 所以他贿赂了他未来岳父的御者，一个叫密耳提洛斯的人——正如你所说，把轮辐换成了……它们叫什么来着，

sentences.en: the axle thing to keep the wheels in with wax.
sentences.zh: 用来固定车轮的轴销换成了蜡。

sentences.en: And so the father dies, Pelops marries, and is a great hero.
sentences.zh: 结果父亲死了，珀罗普斯结了婚，成了一位伟大的英雄。

sentences.en: But he has bribed Myrtalos.
sentences.zh: 但他贿赂了密耳提洛斯。

sentences.en: He's said, you know, I'll give you all kinds of goodies.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，你知道的，我会给你各种各样的好处。

sentences.en: And Myrtalos comes to Pelops for his reward.
sentences.zh: 于是密耳提洛斯来找珀罗普斯索要奖励。

sentences.en: And did you read what Pelops does?
sentences.zh: 你知道珀罗普斯是怎么做的吗？

sentences.en: Does he kill him?
sentences.zh: 他把他杀了吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实杀了。

sentences.en: He chucks him over a cliff.
sentences.zh: 他把他从悬崖上推了下去。

sentences.en: That's harsh, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也太狠了吧？

sentences.en: That's bad form.
sentences.zh: 这人品太差了。

sentences.en: It is harsh.
sentences.zh: 确实很狠。

sentences.en: It's very bad form.
sentences.zh: 人品简直差极了。

sentences.en: So Pelops, you know, he's not a nice guy.
sentences.zh: 所以珀罗普斯，你知道的，他可不是个好人。

sentences.en: No, I'm feeling bad about being in the Peloponnese now.
sentences.zh: 不对，我现在一想到自己身处伯罗奔尼撒，就觉得浑身不得劲。

sentences.en: Well, maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: So Pelops reigns.
sentences.zh: 就这样，珀罗普斯统治了。

sentences.en: It's all great.
sentences.zh: 一切都很美好。

sentences.en: But there is a curse that's been put on his family.
sentences.zh: 但他的家族遭到了诅咒。

sentences.en: And I know you just went to Mycenae, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 我知道你刚刚去了迈锡尼，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, House of Atreus.
sentences.zh: 是的，阿特柔斯家族所在地。

sentences.en: So Atreus is the son of Pelops.
sentences.zh: 所以阿特柔斯是珀罗普斯的儿子。

sentences.en: So Agamemnon, Clytemnestra, Electra, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 因此阿伽门农、克吕泰涅斯特拉、厄勒克特拉，所有这些恩怨。

sentences.en: All that stems from this disastrous chariot race.
sentences.zh: 这一切都源于那场灾难性的战车比赛。

sentences.en: Well, not disastrous for Pelops, but disastrous for his successors.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对珀罗普斯来说不算灾难，但对他的后代却是灾难。

sentences.en: Exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And so you have there the sense that, so in sport, we talk about heroes.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现，在体育运动中，我们常常谈论英雄。

sentences.en: A lot of talk about heroes.
sentences.zh: 有很多关于英雄的讨论。

sentences.en: A hero in Greece is something faintly menacing.
sentences.zh: 但在希腊，英雄带有某种隐隐的威胁意味。

sentences.en: It's someone who kind of has a touch of the divine.
sentences.zh: 那是某种带有神性色彩的人。

sentences.en: And the divine is always dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而神性总是危险的。

sentences.en: So Pelops is not a pleasant guy.
sentences.zh: 所以珀罗普斯并不是个讨人喜欢的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a cheat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是个骗子。

sentences.en: He's really not pleasant at all.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常令人讨厌。

sentences.en: And yet he has something of the strange, something of the kind of demonic in the Greek sense.
sentences.zh: 然而他身上又带着某种奇异的东西，在希腊语境中带有某种近乎恶魔般的特质。

sentences.en: And that sense of the strange and the weird hangs over the games that then kind of emerge.
sentences.zh: 这种奇异和诡异感一直笼罩着后来诞生的运动会。

sentences.en: So there's a sense of the games being expiating sin, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得，运动会有没有一种赎罪的意味？

sentences.en: Is that too strong?
sentences.zh: 这么说是不是有点太过了？

sentences.en: I think that is too strong.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是有点过头了。

sentences.en: I think the key is that the age of heroes has passed.
sentences.zh: 我认为关键在于，英雄的时代已经过去了。

sentences.en: So it passes with the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 它随着特洛伊战争的结束而结束了。

sentences.en: But you come to Olympia and if you're watching the chariot races or the wrestling or whatever,
sentences.zh: 但当你来到奥林匹亚，如果你正在观看战车比赛、摔跤或其他什么，

sentences.en: and you see astounding performances, you are as close to the age of heroes as you possibly can be in the age of iron that we all live in.
sentences.zh: 当你看到那些惊人的表现时，你便尽可能地接近了英雄时代——在我们所有人生活的这个铁器时代里。

sentences.en: And that's the fascination of it, that it's kind of opening up a portal to the weird.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的魅力所在，它就像是开启了一扇通往诡异世界的传送门。

sentences.en: So you've got Zeus is one of the founders, Pelops is the other.
sentences.zh: 所以，宙斯是奠基人之一，珀罗普斯是另一个。

sentences.en: The third one is Heracles, you know, with his 12 labors.
sentences.zh: 第三个是赫拉克勒斯，你知道的，他完成了十二项功绩。

sentences.en: And the other story is that he comes there after he's finished his labors and he institutes the games and he sacrifices a black ram before the tomb of Pelops.
sentences.zh: 另一个传说是，他在完成功绩后离开时创立了运动会，并在珀罗普斯的陵墓前献祭了一头黑公羊。

sentences.en: And this is something that they do every four years of the games.
sentences.zh: 这是他们在每四年举办一次的运动会上都会做的事情。

sentences.en: They sacrifice a ram to Pelops.
sentences.zh: 他们会向珀罗普斯献祭一头公羊。

sentences.en: And, you know, you are kind of taking part in these incredibly vivid stories.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你就像是参与到了这些极其生动的故事中。

sentences.en: They are alive and a part of what you were doing.
sentences.zh: 它们是活生生的，并且是你所做事情的一部分。

sentences.en: And that is absolutely fundamental to everything that the Olympics in antiquity are about.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是古代奥运会一切核心意义的基石。

sentences.en: So just to get away from the myth for a second, where did the idea of games come from?
sentences.zh: 抛开神话不说，运动会的概念究竟是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Is it something the Greeks have got from where have they got it from?
sentences.zh: 这是希腊人从什么地方借鉴来的吗？

sentences.en: From Crete, from Egypt, from Anatolia, or do they invent it?
sentences.zh: 是从克里特、埃及、安纳托利亚学来的，还是他们自己发明的？

sentences.en: Are there games in other places?
sentences.zh: 其他地方也有运动会吗？

sentences.en: I think it's an expression of a kind of obsession with being beSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是对“力争第一”这种执念的一种表达。

sentences.en: So the Greeks can make a contest out of anything.
sentences.zh: 所以希腊人可以把任何事都变成一场比赛。

sentences.en: You know, they can make a contest out of, well, you know, famously plays.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们可以把——比如众所周知的戏剧——变成比赛。

sentences.en: So tragedy and comedies, poetry, but it's kind of beauty contests, weaving.
sentences.zh: 所以悲剧、喜剧、诗歌，还有选美比赛、织布比赛。

sentences.en: I mean, there's absolutely nothing that the Greeks can't make into a conteSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本没有什么是希腊人不能拿来比赛的。

sentences.en: I wouldn't pay to see the weaving conteSt.
sentences.zh: 我可不会花钱去看织布比赛。

sentences.en: But if you're a Greek, you might.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是个希腊人，你可能就会。

sentences.en: And particularly, you know, if it's kind of Athena against Arachne, you know that the loser is going to be turned into a spider.
sentences.zh: 尤其是，你知道的，如果那是雅典娜对决阿拉克涅，你就会知道输的人会被变成蜘蛛。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 这倒也是。

sentences.en: I would pay to, I'd definitely pay to see that.
sentences.zh: 我会花钱去看的，我绝对会花钱去看那个。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's the measure.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是衡量标准。

sentences.en: There's jeopardy in everything.
sentences.zh: 每件事都充满了高风险的悬念。

sentences.en: And it kind of reflects the way in which, you know, the Greeks, you know, they don't have, they have no concept of sport for sport's sake.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上反映了希腊人——你知道的，他们根本没有为运动而运动的概念。

sentences.en: So we were talking about podiuming, the idea of gold, silver and bronze.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚才在讨论领奖台，也就是金、银、铜牌的概念。

sentences.en: But basically, there is no bronze or silver.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，当时没有铜牌或银牌。

sentences.en: You win or you lose.
sentences.zh: 要么赢，要么输。

sentences.en: And when you win, one of the perks you get is you get to commission a kind of victory hymn.
sentences.zh: 当你赢了之后，你能得到的特权之一就是可以委托别人为你创作一首胜利赞歌。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, it's like, I don't know, getting Beyonce or somebody to celebrate your victory in 100 metres, something like that, Rihanna.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你知道的，就像找碧昂丝或者什么人来庆祝你在100米赛跑中获胜，诸如此类，比如蕾哈娜。

sentences.en: And the famous guy who does this in ancient Greece is a guy called Pindar from Thebes.
sentences.zh: 在古希腊，专门做这行最著名的人是一个来自底比斯的叫品达的人。

sentences.en: Is he a playwright, Pindar?
sentences.zh: 品达是个剧作家吗？

sentences.en: No, he writes these odes, these kind of victories, that's what he's chiefly known for.
sentences.zh: 不是，他写这些颂歌，也就是这种胜利赞歌，这正是他最广为人知的成就。
